prompt: You connect your dev board's USB device port directly to the Digitakt's USB port with a suitable cable. Neither sees MIDI from the other. Why?

options.text: Both are USB devices; a USB link needs exactly one host to schedule transfers
options.explanation: Correct. The Digitakt's USB-B socket is meant for a computer host, so it acts as a device. Two devices can't talk to each other.

options.text: USB MIDI is slower than DIN, so messages time out
options.explanation: USB is far faster than 31,250 bit/s. Speed isn't the problem.

options.text: The Digitakt only supports USB audio, not USB MIDI
options.explanation: Both Digitakt models support USB MIDI (USB MIDI or USB AUDIO/MIDI mode). The problem is the missing host.

options.text: A special cable swaps the two device ports into host and device roles
options.explanation: USB has no data cable that swaps the two ends' roles. Roles are fixed by host and device controllers.

workedExample:
1. USB is host-controlled: the host polls devices, and devices only answer.
2. Devices cannot communicate with each other except through a host.
3. The Digitakt's rear USB is a USB-B socket for connecting to a computer host, so it is a device.
4. A dev board's main USB port is normally a device too.
5. Fix: use DIN MIDI, give the synth a USB host port, add a USB MIDI host box, or route through a computer.

link.title: USB On-The-Go (host and device roles) — Wikipedia

prompt: The open questions ask whether the synth must work with the Digitakt **without a computer**. Which connection plans could work? Select all that apply.

options.text: Digitakt MIDI OUT (DIN) to an optocoupler MIDI IN on the synth
options.explanation: Correct. DIN is point to point and needs no host. It is also galvanically isolated.

options.text: Digitakt USB to the synth's ordinary USB device port
options.explanation: Both are devices; without a host nothing can be transferred.

options.text: Digitakt USB to a USB host port on the synth (for example a Teensy 4.1's host port), with host MIDI support in firmware
options.explanation: Correct. The synth then acts as host and the Digitakt as a device. Confirm in your Digitakt model's manual that its USB MIDI mode suits this.

options.text: Both devices plugged into a standalone USB MIDI host box that forwards between them
options.explanation: Correct. The box provides the host role.

options.text: A USB-C to USB-C cable between them, because USB-C is symmetric
options.explanation: Connector symmetry does not create a USB host. One end must support and run the host role; the other may be an ordinary device. Digitakt has a USB-B device-side connector.

workedExample:
Ask of each plan: "who is the host?"

1. DIN MIDI: no host concept; works.
2. Device to device: no host; fails.
3. Synth as host: works if your board has a host port and you write or use host MIDI firmware.
4. Host box: the box is the host; works.
5. Connector shape: irrelevant to roles. (The Digitakt has a USB-B socket, which is a device-side connector.)

DIN is the simplest first build; USB host is a possible later feature.

link.title: USB On-The-Go (host and device roles) — Wikipedia
